Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo dell'0,83%, Shanghai in rialzo dello 0,38%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

L'S&P 500 è in calo del 0,32% a settanta‑settecentoventidue punti, il VIX in ribasso dell'1,16% a quindici virgola ventotto, il DXY in rialzo dello 0,06% a novantanove virgola ottantotto. L'oro è in rialzo dell'1,74% a quattro‑mila‑quattro‑cento‑cinquantanove dollari l'oncia, segnale di protezione contro l'inflazione. Il petrolio Brent sale dello 0,29% a ottantanove virgola diciassette dollari, riflesso di domanda costante. Il rendimento del US 10Y è in calo dello 0,32% a quattro virgola sessantotto percento, indicando aspettative di inflazione più basse. Il BTP 10Y resta stabile al tre virgola settantatré percento. Il TLT 20Y è in rialzo dello 0,16% a ottantadue virgola diciannove, conferma di flusso verso titoli a lungo termine.

Sul fronte geopolitico, le tensioni in Ucraina aumentano dopo il rimescolamento dei leader militari da parte di Zelenskyy, mantenendo pressione sui prezzi dell'energia. Parallelamente, la Russia intensifica la retorica anti‑occidentale, potenziale fonte di volatilità nei mercati energetici.

Macro e banche centrali: oggi sono in programma i dati CPI YoY e Core CPI YoY degli Stati Uniti. Nessun altro dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin registra una lieve flessione dello 0,4 percento, attestandosi a sessantatremila cinquecento novantatré dollari, mentre i flussi netti degli ETF mostrano un deflusso di centotrentaquattro virgola sei milioni di dollari. Ethereum registra un rialzo dello 0,7 percento, quotandosi a duemilacentottantacinque dollari. Binance Coin avanza del due virgola zero quattro percento, posizionandosi a seicento dieci virgola quattro nove dollari, ed è l’unico altcoin con movimento significativo sopra il due percento. Il Fear & Greed Index segna ventisette, in zona paura, suggerendo cautela sugli investitori.

Oggi monitoriamo i dati CPI YoY e Core CPI YoY degli USA, fondamentali per i mercati. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing.

The Nikkei closed up 0.83%, Shanghai up 0.38%. This suggests a weak opening for European markets.

The S&P 500 is down 0.32% at 7,722 points, the VIX down 1.16% at 15.28, the DXY up 0.06% at 99.88. Gold is up 1.74% at $4,459 per ounce, a signal of inflation protection. Brent crude rises 0.29% to $89.17, reflecting steady demand. The US 10Y yield is down 0.32% at 4.68%, indicating lower inflation expectations. The 10Y Italian BTP is flat at 3.73%. The TLT 20Y is up 0.16% at 82.19, confirming flow into long‑term bonds.

On the geopolitical front, tensions in Ukraine rise after Zelenskyy reshuffles military leadership, keeping pressure on energy prices. Meanwhile, Russia ramps up anti‑Western rhetoric, a potential source of volatility in energy markets.

Macro and central banks: today’s agenda includes US CPI YoY and Core CPI YoY data. No other major macro releases are expected.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin slips 0.4% to $63,593, while net ETF flows show an outflow of $134.6 million. Ethereum rises 0.7% to $2,285. Binance Coin gains 2.04% to $610.49, the only altcoin with a move above two percent. The Fear & Greed Index sits at 27, in fear territory, suggesting investor caution.

articles.title: Africa's public debt amid global headwinds: balancing resilience and vulnerabilities
articles.snippet: by Michael Chui, Leonardo Gambacorta The conflict in the Middle East has raised energy and fertiliser prices, weakened growth and intensified fiscal pressures across Africa at a time when public debt and debt service burdens remain elevated. The shift towards domestic currency debt has reduced exchange rate risk for issuers and preserved market access, but higher interest rates and shorter maturities have increased debt service costs and rollover risks. A heavy reliance on banks and central banks for government financing can reinforce the sovereign-bank nexus, crowd out private credit and threaten financial stability. Developing deeper markets and a more diversified investor base are essential to address these challenges.

articles.title: Putting Armageddon on Autopilot: How Artificial Intelligence Could Make Nuclear Threats More Effective
articles.snippet: Nine countries now possess nuclear weapons. Arms control agreements painstakingly built over decades have collapsed. Geopolitical competition is intensifying rivalries between nuclear-armed powers. North Korea continues expanding its arsenal and delivery systems. China is on a trajectory to go from roughly 600 warheads today to around 1,500 by 2035. Meanwhile, Russia bears most of the responsibility for the expiration of New START and is developing an array of exotic new nuclear delivery systems designed to circumvent missile defenses. This includes nuclear-powered and nuclear-armed cruise missiles and underwater drones, hypersonic glide vehicles, and a nuclear-armed anti-satellite weapon. articles.title: Who Pays for America’s Research and Development?
articles.snippet: When the Soviet Union launched Sputnik in 1957, the U.S. government was the unrivaled patron of American science. It funded nearly two-thirds of the nation’s research and development — much of it for defense — defining the early Cold War. In a phenomenon that’s been widely explored in our Arsenal of Innovation series, for several decades federal dollars pushed the technological frontier, and the private sector followed.Today, that arrangement has been inverted. articles.title: Middle East War Pushes China Toward the Arctic Trade Route
articles.snippet: The Middle East conflict and the heightened threats to shipping in the Red Sea have prompted China to boost the use of the Arctic to move containers from the Chinese east coast to Europe. The fast-melting Arctic ice offers an alternative shipping route in the summer as the Houthi threats to shipping in the Red Sea and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait make cargo operators more cautious in transiting the key chokepoints in the Middle East. Shipping through the Arctic is not something new, but this time around – driven by melting ice caps and more dangerous…

articles.title: IEA Numbers Point to a Two-Speed Recovery in Global Fuel Prices
articles.snippet: Five months after the U.S. and Israel opened a war with Iran, global fuel markets still haven't settled down, and the latest IEA data prove it. The IEA's monthly end-use price tracker, updated Aug. 7 and covering prices through July, shows the average per-liter cost of automotive diesel across the countries it tracks sitting near $1.94 in U.S. dollar terms.
